title: Command-Line Interface Design with argparse
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and value of Command-Line Interface Design with argparse.
Apply command-line interface design with argparse to a Python project scenario.
Identify decisions and trade-offs relevant to command-line interface design with argparse.
Review common mistakes and risks in command-line interface design with argparse.
Produce a verifiable project artifact using command-line interface design with argparse principles.

understand.concept: A command-line interface accepts arguments, options and commands from a terminal. The argparse module parses these inputs, provides help text and reports invalid arguments. Good CLI design uses clear names, predictable exit codes and safe defaults.
understand.whyItMatters: A well-designed CLI makes Python tools scriptable, automatable and easier to operate.
understand.analogy: A control panel labels each switch and explains what it changes.
understand.analogyLimit: CLI parsing does not validate every business rule or grant authorization; those checks belong in application logic.
understand.summary: Command-Line Interface Design with argparse helps learners deliver and maintain reliable Python projects.

explain.narrative: Use argparse to define positional arguments, optional flags, types, defaults and subcommands. Keep parsing separate from business logic so functions can be tested directly. Provide meaningful help, validate domain constraints after parsing and return appropriate exit statuses. Avoid destructive defaults.

examples.title: Parse a positional argument
examples.code:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('filename')
args = parser.parse_args(['report.csv'])
print(args.filename)
examples.explanation: A positional argument supplies a required value.

examples.title: Parse a typed option
examples.code:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--limit', type=int, default=10)
args = parser.parse_args(['--limit', '5'])
print(args.limit)
examples.explanation: The type option converts and validates basic argument syntax.

examples.title: Use a boolean flag
examples.code:
import argparse
parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
parser.add_argument('--dry-run', action='store_true')
print(parser.parse_args(['--dry-run']).dry_run)
examples.explanation: A store_true flag is false unless supplied.

examples.title: Check a parsed value
examples.explanation: Business constraints should be checked after parsing.

examples.title: Return a clear status
examples.explanation: A zero exit status conventionally indicates success.
